papers.title: Narwhal and Tusk: A DAG-based Mempool and Efficient BFT Consensus
papers.summary: We propose separating the task of reliable transaction dissemination from transaction ordering, to enable high-performance Byzantine fault-tolerant quorum-based consensus. We design and evaluate a mempool protocol, Narwhal, specializing in high-throughput reliable dissemination and storage of causal histories of transactions. Narwhal tolerates an asynchronous network and maintains high performance despite failures.

papers.title: Bullshark: DAG BFT Protocols Made Practical
papers.summary: We present Bullshark, the first directed acyclic graph (DAG) based Byzantine Atomic Broadcast protocol that is optimized for the common synchronous case. Like previous DAG-based BFT protocols, Bullshark requires no extra communication to achieve consensus on top of building the DAG.

papers.title: Bullshark: The Partially Synchronous Version
papers.summary: A partially synchronous simplification of Bullshark, the DAG-based BFT atomic broadcast protocol, presenting a simpler and more direct construction that still preserves the practical performance benefits of the original.

papers.title: SoK: Diving into DAG-based Blockchain Systems
papers.summary: A systematization of knowledge covering DAG-based distributed ledger systems, surveying consensus mechanisms, design tradeoffs, and open problems across the DAG-blockchain literature.

papers.title: Imitater: An Efficient Shared Mempool Protocol with Application to Byzantine Fault Tolerance
papers.summary: We propose a novel Shared Mempool (SMP) protocol, named Imitater, which can be seamlessly integrated into BFT protocols. By chaining microblocks and applying coding techniques, Imitater efficiently achieves totality and availability. Furthermore, a BFT protocol augmented with Imitater ensures order preservation of client transactions while mitigating the risks of over-distribution and unbalanced workload.

papers.title: On the Design of Ethereum's Data Availability Sampling
papers.summary: A design analysis of Ethereum's Data Availability Sampling (DAS), the erasure-coded scheme (a tensor code of two Reed-Solomon codes over a k-by-k matrix) proposed for danksharding, letting light nodes verify blob data availability by sampling without downloading the whole blob.
